keyFindings.description: The ci-filters check is red at the CI head 0fbea003 with 30 problems. The jobs test, docs, dispatch, dispatch-browser-multiprocess and envoy-infra-go all read the new packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/itemblocks/*.go files (through go build ./cmd/dispatch and the docs binaries), but none of their path filters matches that directory. So a later change to itemblocks alone would skip those jobs. main does not share this red: main has no itemblocks. Fix: add 'packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/itemblocks/*' to each of those five filters in ci.yaml, beside the other internal/dispatch packages, and run .github/scripts/check-ci-filters.sh.

The ids are worked out from a different body than the one Save sends. composedRequest computes carriedIdsOf(followedBlocks.current, body) from the React state, and sentRequest then sends textarea.current?.value ?? body. Before round 9 the ids were checked against the sent body. Reachable path: open an edit of a comment whose stored body has CR LF, then save without typing. body keeps the CR LF (replaceDraft(editBody)), while the textarea and followed.value hold LF, so carriedBlocks returns undefined and the save carries no ids. deep-review reproduced this with a CR LF-normalizing textarea: round 8's code sent base_revision 3 and b1/b2, the head sent {body} alone. Fix: in sentRequest, read the textarea value once and use it for both draft.body and edit.carried. Add a test with a CR LF comment and a CR LF-normalizing textarea, which fails at the head.

carriedIdsOf's doc comment still says "The block ids `sent`'s save carries ... None for a send that is no edit", but it no longer takes `sent`. The finding above touches the same code, so fix this wording with it.
